# Department of Defense outlays (in millions) from FY 2011 to FY 2020
data = [678077, 650869, 607801, 578013, 562506, 565365, 568905, 600705, 653979, 690420]

# Sort the data
sorted_data = sorted(data)
print("Sorted data:", sorted_data)

# Hazen plotting position formula: P = (m - 0.2) / (n + 0.2)
# For 85th percentile, we need P = 0.85
# Solving for m: m = 0.85 * (n + 0.2) + 0.2
n = len(sorted_data)
print(f"\nn = {n}")

# Calculate m for 85th percentile
m_85 = 0.85 * (n + 0.2) + 0.2
print(f"m for 85th percentile: {m_85}")

# The percentile falls between rank 8 and rank 9
# Let's verify the plotting positions
for i, val in enumerate(sorted_data, 1):
    p = (i - 0.2) / (n + 0.2)
    print(f"Rank {i}, Value {val}, P = {p:.4f}")

# Linear interpolation for 85th percentile
# Between rank 8 (value = 600705) and rank 9 (value = 650869)
rank_below = 8
rank_above = 9
value_below = sorted_data[rank_below - 1]
value_above = sorted_data[rank_above - 1]

# P8 = (8-0.2)/(10+0.2) = 7.8/10.2 = 0.7647
# P9 = (9-0.2)/(10+0.2) = 8.8/10.2 = 0.8627
p8 = (rank_below - 0.2) / (n + 0.2)
p9 = (rank_above - 0.2) / (n + 0.2)

print(f"\nP8 = {p8:.4f}, P9 = {p9:.4f}")

# Interpolate to find value at P = 0.85
# Using linear interpolation: y = y1 + (x - x1) * (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)
percentile_85 = value_below + (0.85 - p8) * (value_above - value_below) / (p9 - p8)

print(f"\n85th Hazen Percentile: {percentile_85}")
print(f"Rounded to nearest hundredth: {round(percentile_85, 2)}")
